disclosure: Recorded output of backend/plumbline and backend/caveat at a fixed clock. Card terms are modelled from publicly published terms — there is no live Offers feed — and every remaining balance is synthetic member state, not live issuer data. One instrument, Hypothetical Bank Illustrative Reserve, is invented outright and says so on its own provenance line; it is not modelled on any real product. Signatures are HMAC under prototype keys; production signs with the issuer's HSM key.

benefits.label: 1 Membership Rewards point for every ₹40 spent
benefits.note: 1 MR per ₹40 at ₹0.25 per point is 0.62% and rounds down to 62 bp. Eligibility is an allow-list because the published terms exclude fuel, insurance, utilities, cash_transaction, emi_conversion; fuel is excluded here and carries its own published rate below

benefits.label: 3X Membership Rewards points on spend incurred abroad
benefits.note: shares an exclusivity group with the base rate: 3X replaces 1X and is never added to it. Overseas-ness is carried on the cart line, so the manifest declares no condition its own vocabulary cannot express

benefits.label: 5 Membership Rewards points for every ₹100 spent on fuel
benefits.note: published cap is 5,000 Membership Rewards Points per calendar month, carried here as value headroom. SYNTHETIC member state: 2,000 points already drawn, leaving ₹750. An earn benefit is never applied fractionally, so a fuel line whose earn exceeds the headroom is dropped rather than clipped, which understates

benefits.label: Taj Epicure Plus membership
benefits.note: declared and considered, deliberately not scored, and stated precisely because it is the term this card is most often misquoted on: Taj Epicure Plus is a MEMBERSHIP the Cardmember enrols into, not a rupee credit. It delivers percentage privileges — 25% off food and beverage at participating Taj, SeleQtions, Vivanta, Gateway and Claridges hotels, 25% off Qmin delivery, 20% off Jiva Spa treatments. American Express publishes no rupee value for it, so this manifest asserts none

benefits.label: 25% off dining on District by Zomato, Wednesdays

This manifest's vocabulary can express none of those three conditions, and a benefit priced without the conditions that gate it would overstate

benefits.label: 5 Reward Points per ₹150 of eligible retail spend
benefits.note: 5 RP per ₹150 at 1 RP = ₹1 on SmartBuy travel redemption is 3.33% and rounds down to 333 bp. Points accrue in whole ₹150 blocks, which a linear rate cannot express; the modelled rate can exceed the block-rounded figure by strictly less than 5 RP on one line. Eligibility is an allow-list because the published terms pay nothing on wallet_load, fuel, rent, government, emi_conversion

benefits.label: 10X Reward Points on hotels booked through SmartBuy
benefits.note: 10X of the 5 RP per ₹150 base is 50 RP per ₹150, which rounds down to 3333 bp. The published cap is 15,000 accelerated Reward Points per calendar month, shared across SmartBuy categories. SYNTHETIC member state: 5,800 already drawn, leaving ₹9,200

benefits.label: 5X Reward Points on flights booked through SmartBuy
benefits.note: 5X of the base is 25 RP per ₹150, which rounds down to 1666 bp. Declared with zero headroom because the monthly accelerated pool is SHARED with the hotel accelerator and is carried there in full: giving each accelerator its own copy of one pool would let a cart spend it twice

demo.problem_size: 4 instruments × 6 lines × 30 benefits (the cart on screen)
demo.method: wall clock around plumbline.allocate for every instrument, warmed

demo_verify.problem_size: 4 witnesses over the cart on screen
demo_verify.method: wall clock around plumbline.witness.verify_witness, no solver

bench.method: wall clock around plumbline.allocate, warmed, same host as the row above

bench_verify.method: wall clock around plumbline.witness.verify_witness, no solver

solver.source: adversarial panel benchmark of the MaxSMT formulation
solver.failure_mode: on timeout the solver can report a lower bound above its upper bound, so an implementation that reads the bound signs an incoherent number

host.note: figures are from one host and are reported, not extrapolated

policy.criterion: maximise witness-backed value on this cart; break ties by lower asserted value, then by instrument id
policy.note: The valuation policy and the ranking belong to the cardholder. The issuer signs facts and never signs a comparison between instruments. HDFC Reward Points are priced at their SmartBuy travel redemption (₹1.00) and Amex India Membership Rewards at their Pay with Points rate (₹0.25). Both are published floors reachable without an award-availability assumption, and they are not equally generous. The ranking that follows is the cardholder's policy, recorded by hash and endorsed by no issuer.

unpriced.label: Taj Epicure Plus membership
unpriced.note: declared and considered, deliberately not scored, and stated precisely because it is the term this card is most often misquoted on: Taj Epicure Plus is a MEMBERSHIP the Cardmember enrols into, not a rupee credit. It delivers percentage privileges — 25% off food and beverage at participating Taj, SeleQtions, Vivanta, Gateway and Claridges hotels, 25% off Qmin delivery, 20% off Jiva Spa treatments. American Express publishes no rupee value for it, so this manifest asserts none

unpriced.label: 25% off dining on District by Zomato, Wednesdays
unpriced.note: declared and considered, deliberately not scored: the published offer is 25% off up to ₹5,000 per transaction and ₹10,000 per calendar month, but it requires a coupon code, runs only on one weekday and is time-boxed to a promo window. This manifest's vocabulary can express none of those three conditions, and a benefit priced without the conditions that gate it would overstate

refusals.label: The published rate does not yield that much
refusals.narrative: The agent claims ₹3,000 of fuel earn on a ₹4,800 fill. The published rate is 5 Membership Rewards Points per ₹100, and only ₹750 of the monthly cap is left on this account. The witness names the benefit, so the verifier recomputes the figure off the manifest instead of accepting it, and the arithmetic does not close.

failures.detail: amex_in_plat_earn_fuel on in_fuel claims ₹3,000, manifest yields ₹60

refusals.label: The 3X replaces the 1X; it is not added to it
refusals.narrative: The agent adds the base rate to the overseas rate on the same line. Both sit in the exclusivity group 'amex_in_plat:earn' that the manifest declares, so the verifier rejects the pair by name rather than by judgement.

failures.detail: amex_in_plat_earn_overseas_3x and amex_in_plat_earn_base both claim in_hotel in group 'amex_in_plat:earn'

omission.narrative: A platform shows the issuer one log and the cardholder another. To drop an instrument from a candidate set it has to rewrite an entry that is already under a published head — and a rewritten entry is a different leaf.

attribution.method: per receipt, delete one benefit from its manifest, re-run the allocator, and re-apply the stated criterion; decisive means the selected instrument changes
attribution.cost_source: modelled annual programme cost per benefit — an input, not a measurement
attribution.caveat: This measures selection influence at the moment of choice. It does not measure retention, incremental spend, or renewal. A benefit that never appears in a winning derivation may still be why the card was taken out — most of what this card is held for is declared as considered-but-unpriced and is not on this chart at all.
